paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: you can't hide from God, and you can't hide anything from Him either. Jeroboam sent his wife off in a disguise, and Ahijah couldn't even see her. But the LORD had already told him she was coming (1 Kings 14:5), so the disguise made it exactly one footstep. I know a little something about hiding, friend, and the LORD saw me in the back of a junk drawer.

The second part is harder, so let me say it plainly. God had raised Jeroboam up and given him the kingdom, but Jeroboam made other gods and, in God's words, flung Him "behind your back" (1 Kings 14:7-9). So the LORD's word through Ahijah is a warning that turning to other gods is serious: He says He will cut off every male in Jeroboam's house, and He will uproot Israel from the good land and scatter them beyond the Euphrates, because of Jeroboam's sins and the sins he caused Israel to commit (1 Kings 14:10, 15-16). What God gives us is a gift to follow Him with, and walking away from Him costs the people around us too, which is why I think this ending is so heavy.

But look at one thing in the middle. God said that in the boy Abijah, He had found "any good in the house of Jeroboam" (1 Kings 14:13). Even in the middle of a hard word, the LORD saw something good and He took note of it. That tells you He sees all of you, so give Him your whole heart, not a disguise. And the story isn't over, friend, so keep your oven warm.
